scope: Proposed statistical methods for future matched site inventories and effort-based discovery curves; no fitted Indus totals
raw_handling: Local-only acquired primary PDFs and extracted text; authored notes and metadata may be tracked

sources.authors: U.S. Census Bureau, Coverage Measurement Design and Estimation Integrated Project Team
sources.title: 2020 Post-Enumeration Survey: Estimation Design
sources.publication: DSSD 2020 Post-Enumeration Survey Memorandum Series #2020-J-03, 29 November 2022
sources.access_depth: Full 82-page PDF acquired; targeted model, independence, heterogeneity and matching sections inspected
sources.locator: §3.1–3.2, printed pp.3–8, PDF pp.8–13; §3.6–3.9, printed pp.15–20, PDF pp.20–25
sources.observation: Dual-system estimation depends on inclusion independence. Operational dependence and heterogeneous inclusion can produce correlation bias; records must be correctly included and matched.
sources.limits: Census operational design is a methodological reference, not evidence of archaeological population size or survey independence

sources.title: The multiple recapture census for closed populations and incomplete 2^k contingency tables
sources.access_depth: Primary publisher-indexed abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; direct article open failed; full paper not acquired
sources.locator: Publisher abstract, multinomial capture histories and log-linear projection to missing cell
sources.observation: Multiple capture histories form an incomplete contingency table; fitted log-linear models project to the all-zero cell to estimate total population.
sources.limits: Supports the method outline, not a reanalysis of its full derivation; proposed application still requires dependence restrictions and valid matching

sources.title: Nonidentifiability of Population Size from Capture-Recapture Data with Heterogeneous Detection Probabilities
sources.access_depth: Full primary publisher landing page, abstract and official USGS bibliographic record inspected; full article not acquired
sources.locator: Primary abstract, reasonable alternative heterogeneity models and essentially identical observations
sources.observation: Different plausible detection-heterogeneity models can produce essentially indistinguishable observations while implying substantially different population sizes, even with large samples.
sources.limits: Full mathematical derivation not read; zero-detection construction in the authored note is a separate algebraic illustration

sources.authors: Robert K. Colwell, Chang Xuan Mao, Jing Chang
sources.title: Interpolating, Extrapolating, and Comparing Incidence-Based Species Accumulation Curves
sources.access_depth: Full published 11-page PDF from author-linked host acquired; introduction, model, interpolation and discussion passages inspected
sources.locator: Printed pp.2717–2719, sampling units and model assumptions; p.2726, extrapolation and asymptote limitations
sources.observation: Comparable incidence samples support interpolation and limited extrapolation using detection frequencies; the presented extrapolation is unreliable for estimating the ultimate richness asymptote.
sources.limits: Ecological species-incidence model requires an explicit archaeological adaptation; annual list totals or disjoint site tiles do not automatically supply the required histories

sources.title: Coverage-based rarefaction and extrapolation: standardizing samples by completeness rather than size
sources.access_depth: Full primary publisher article available through web tool; coverage definition, sampling-curve methods and discussion inspected; no local full-text witness acquired
sources.locator: Sample Coverage and the Species Accumulation Curve; Coverage-Based Extrapolation; Discussion
sources.observation: Coverage describes represented probability mass and supports comparisons of sample completeness; limited sampling cannot establish every rare identity or an ultimate richness ranking.
sources.limits: The paper's individual-based formulas are not directly applicable to archaeological incidence data without choosing an appropriate model and sampling units
